## Left-Aligning Table Captions in LaTeX (Without `caption` Package)

Here are several approaches:

---

### Method 1: Redefine `\fnum@table` and use `\raggedright`

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \raggedright #1: #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother
```

Place this in your **preamble**.

---

### Method 2: Using a `minipage`

Wrap your caption inside a `minipage` that spans the full width:

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
    \centering
    \begin{tabular}{cc}
        A & B \\
    \end{tabular}
    \begin{minipage}{\textwidth}
        \caption{Your caption here}
    \end{minipage}
\end{table}
```

---

### Method 3: Redefine `\flushleft` for captions in preamble

```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@makecaption}[2]{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \begin{flushleft}
    #1: #2
  \end{flushleft}
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother
```

---

### Simplest Quick Fix (Per Table)

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
\raggedright          % <-- add this
\caption{Your caption}
\centering            % <-- re-center the table itself
\begin{tabular}{cc}
    A & B \\
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

> **Note:** `\raggedright` before `\caption` affects the caption, and `\centering` after re-centers the tabular content.

---

**Method 1 or 3** are the most robust as they apply globally to all captions.
